sources: dossier=Net position bullet 2 + Required behaviors bullet 1 ('every request gets a synthetic admin identity', corroborated 2026-05-15 control-plane-mcp-and-auth + 2026-06-08 corpus-bootstrap); doc=anonymous-mode.md:12 'every request — including requests with no Authorization header — is admitted as a synthetic admin identity'; code=auth_middleware.go resolveIdentity (h=="" branch only substitutes AnonymousIdentity; a present-but-malformed/unknown/expired/revoked Bearer always yields DenialInvalidToken/DenialRevokedToken/DenialExpiredToken regardless of IsAnonymousMode, i.e. 401 even with zero active keys); test=no scenario or unit test exercises a malformed/stale bearer token during zero-active-key state either way.
note: User ruling 2026-07-17 (design-call resolved, option A): anonymous-mode admission is scoped to credential-less requests only; presented-but-bad tokens are rejected 401 in every mode — fail closed, tell the client its token is bad rather than silently promoting it to synthetic admin. Doc narrowed, dossier updated; code already conforms.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors ('TTL is the only freshness mechanism, no cross-process invalidation channel', 2026-05-15 control-plane-mcp-and-auth) and Intentional absences ('No cross-process cache-invalidation channel for the anonymous predicate — the TTL bounds staleness by design'); doc=anonymous-mode.md:28 listed 'sweep' alongside create/revoke/rotate as a same-replica-immediate cache invalidation; code=runAuthSweepLoop runs only in the scheduler role (scheduler.go), RegisterAuthMutationHook is only called from control-api startup (controlapi.go:201) against a process-local hook slice (auth_sweep.go), so a split-deployment scheduler's sweep never reaches any control-api replica's cache; ActiveCount (api_keys.go:124-133) already excludes rows whose revoke_at has passed, so sweep's revoked_at stamping cannot change the predicate regardless.
note: The doc overstated what the rotation-grace sweep does to the anonymous predicate's cache. Fixed anonymous-mode.md to drop 'sweep' from the same-replica-invalidating mutation list and state that the sweep is irrelevant to the predicate because the active-key count already excludes revoke_at-passed rows, matching the dossier's design intent that TTL (not a sweep-driven channel) bounds cross-process staleness.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 3 ('subsequent unauthenticated requests are refused', 2026-06-08 corpus-bootstrap) states the blanket-refusal framing the doc echoes; design corpus=story rimsky-health-check asserts the health probe must remain reachable without a bearer token; doc=anonymous-mode.md:39 (pre-fix) 'subsequent unauthenticated requests are rejected as unauthorized' with no scoping; test=test/scenarios/health_check_e2e_test.go FALSIFIER pins GET /v1/health returning 2xx with no Authorization header after anonymous mode closes.
note: A durable story plus its scenario falsifier establish that health/status probes are deliberately never identity-gated, so the dossier's blanket 'refused' language describes identity-gated requests, not literally every unauthenticated request. Fixed anonymous-mode.md step 6 to scope the refusal to identity-gated requests and note that never-authenticated routes are unaffected.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors ('rimsky auth init calls POST /auth/keys unauthenticated while anonymous ... the server predicate, not the CLI check, is the gate', 2026-05-15 control-plane-mcp-and-auth) confirms a single mint path; doc=anonymous-mode.md Purpose ('the same endpoint operators use thereafter') vs Bootstrap sequence step 3 (pre-fix) 'via the unauthenticated endpoint', which reads as a distinct bootstrap-only route; code=cmd/rimsky/cli/auth_init.go posts to the same /v1/auth/keys route handleCreateKey serves for authenticated mints, with an empty credential.
note: Internal doc inconsistency: Purpose already states there is one mint endpoint, but step 3's phrasing implied a separate 'unauthenticated endpoint'. Fixed anonymous-mode.md step 3 to describe the request as unauthenticated rather than the endpoint, consistent with Purpose and the dossier's single-mint-path confirmation.
